page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance within the Dplsv6 family, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon, providing 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs clocked at 3.4 GHz alongside 128 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no local storage drives, requiring external premium network storage, and contains zero GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate top-tier memory subsystem throughput alongside strong multi-core compute capability. Uncached memory bandwidth tests record read speeds of 449.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 188.51 GB/sec, matching top-tier evaluations in PassMark memory testing. Multi-core performance is robust, showing top-quartile results across stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench 6 multi-core, and Clang software compilation benchmarks. Operational tests report 61.87 million operations per second in Redis SET tasks and 50.4 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register within mid-range averages, and prompt processing for large 70B language models falls into lower percentiles.

The 2.0 GB per core configuration reflects a compute-dense profile that avoids surplus memory overhead, offering qualitative cost efficiency for high-concurrency tasks. However, workloads requiring heavy single-thread performance, extensive per-core RAM, or integrated NVMe storage must account for the platform constraints. The server is well aligned for multi-threaded build environments, high-throughput web frontends, parallel ETL processes, and Redis caching nodes.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is a compute-dense virtual machine powered by a 32-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Offering 32 dedicated vCPUs with 128 MB of L3 cache and 64.0 GB of memory, it operates at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server features no local storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on remote network-attached disks for persistence. Empirical benchmark data indicates top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 449 GB/sec read and 188 GB/sec write speeds, complementing strong multi-threaded execution in Clang compilation and PassMark database operations. Redis throughput reaches 61.87 million operations per second, with web serving reaching 50.4 GB/sec. Although single-core scores and large-model inference remain average to low, the instance provides cost-efficient multi-threaded compute density suited for software compilation, web serving, CI/CD runners, and distributed in-memory caching.
